The midterm elections this month saw a Democratic blowout of GOP candidates even in deep-red territory — and now, one tech figure who once buddied up to President Trump seems to be changing his tune accordingly.

Palantir CEO Alex Karp, in a new interview with Politico, bragged about his lefty bona fides and claimed he’d back a Democrat for president, sparking widespread mockery for the seemingly shameless flip-flop.

“I’ve been a Democrat my whole life. I grew up in a far left environment. I know more about being a progressive than almost anybody on the planet, and I absolutely believe Palantir — all of our products are essentially progressive,” Karp said.

It was only a year ago that many had viewed him as a right-wing ally.

Karp’s company Palantir Technologies, a secretive data analytics giant, had contracts with the Trump Administration that included assisting Immigration and Customs Enforcement and the now-shuttered Department of Government Efficiency.

He even claimed that his company was the first to be “completely anti-woke” last year, alongside multiple instances where he has defended Republican President Trump.

The New Hampshire-born tech exec even once blasted the Dems as “completely irresponsible.”

“He has clearly shifted to the right, although he would probably say that he didn’t leave the left — the left left him,” Michael Steinberger, author of “The Philosopher in the Valley,” told The New York Post last year.

But now, after the midterms, Karp told Politico that Democrats “absolutely” corrected in 2026 enough to win back his support in 2028.

The data analytics boss, who’s worth an estimated $18 billion, clarified he will not back any member of the Democratic Socialists of America. But he also mused to Politico about the failures of capitalism.

“‘What are you gonna do about economic justice in this country?’ And I would say the Democrats have an advantage here because for many Republicans there’s an orthodoxy that capitalism solves all problems,” Karp said.

“Maybe that was once true. I never thought it was true. It’s definitely not true now. And so basically everyone center, center-left understands this,” he added.

Karp said Trump made mistakes in his second term, pointing to the president’s recent remarks that his immigration policy went too far.

“I’m glad he’s saying in public now what I’ve been saying in private,” Karp claimed.

The tech titan’s shifting political allegiance had many in the public and on social media disgusted with what they perceived as opportunism.

“Did he make a comment remotely close to this in the last 3 years? What a pandering POS,” wrote one user.

“Oh… tech sociopath who has been sucking up to Trump is now considering backing Democrats?How very opportunistic of Karp!” another said.

Many noted that since his company relies heavily on government contracts, it only made business sense for him to please whoever is in power.

But the switcheroo may not work, warned one user by the name of Thomas Chadowski.

“The Democrats are still coming after you for supporting DHS and we won’t forget you walking back your support for immigration enforcement,” he said.
news.content: در نتایج جستجوی خود، پوشش خبری بیشتری از ما را مشاهده کنید. در انتخابات میان‌دوره‌ای این ماه، دموکرات‌ها حتی در مناطق کاملاً جمهوری‌خواه، پیروزی قاطعانه‌ای بر نامزدهای حزب جمهوری‌خواه کسب کردند - و اکنون، به نظر می‌رسد یکی از چهره‌های فعال در حوزه فناوری که زمانی با رئیس‌جمهور ترامپ روابط دوستانه‌ای داشت، در حال تغییر موضع خود متناسب با این شرایط است. الکس کارپ، مدیر عامل Palantir، در مصاحبه جدیدی با Politico، به صداقت چپ‌گرایانه خود فخر فروخت و ادعا کرد که از یک دموکرات برای ریاست جمهوری حمایت خواهد کرد، و این تغییر موضع ظاهراً بی‌شرمانه باعث تمسخر گسترده او شد.«من در تمام عمرم دموکرات بوده‌ام. من در محیطی کاملاً چپ‌گرا بزرگ شدم. من بیشتر از تقریباً هر کسی روی کره زمین درباره مترقی بودن می‌دانم و کاملاً معتقدم که Palantir — همه محصولات ما اساساً مترقی هستند.» تنها یک سال پیش بود که بسیاری او را متحد جناح راست می‌دانستند. شرکت کارپ، Palantir Technologies، یک غول مخفی تحلیل داده‌ها، قراردادهایی با دولت ترامپ داشت که شامل کمک به اداره مهاجرت و گمرک و وزارتخانه اکنون تعطیل‌شده کارآیی دولت بود. او حتی ادعا کرد که شرکتش اولین شرکتی بود که سال گذشته «کاملاً ضد بیداری» بود، و در کنار آن موارد متعددی وجود داشت که در آنها از رئیس‌جمهور جمهوری‌خواه، ترامپ، دفاع کرده بود. این مدیر اجرایی فناوری که متولد نیوهمپشایر است، حتی یک بار دموکرات‌ها را «کاملاً بی‌مسئولیت» خواند. مایکل اشتاین‌برگر، نویسنده کتاب «فیلسوف در دره»، سال گذشته به نیویورک پست گفت: «او به وضوح به سمت راست متمایل شده است، اگرچه احتمالاً می‌گوید که چپ را ترک نکرده است — بلکه چپ او را ترک کرده است.»

For a technology that involves doing absolutely nothing but basking in some light rays, red light therapy (RLT) is wildly effective.

Whether you’re treating acne, thickening hair, softening fine lines, speeding muscle recovery, or just looking to biohack your way to a better mood, red light has entered the chat. Once reserved for dermatologists and expensive med spas, at-home RLT devices now come in all shapes, sizes, and wavelengths.

What makes red light therapy so powerful? It works at the cellular level, stimulating mitochondria (the energy powerhouses of your cells) to produce more ATP (adenosine triphosphate), the fuel your body uses to repair itself. That translates to brighter skin, faster muscle recovery, and even improved sleep.

Studies suggest stacking red light therapy with methylene blue — yes, that vivid blue liquid with fans including RFK Jr. going viral for its nootropic benefits — can supercharge results by enhancing mitochondrial function even further. Think of it as adding rocket fuel to your already glowing engine.

So whether you’re a fitness junkie, a skincare maximalist, or just want to look hotter and live longer (don’t we all?), here are the best red light therapy devices worth investing in.

Red light has rejuvenating properties that should not go unnoticed — this full-body panel is no exception. The clinical-grade device emits healing wavelengths from 630 nm at the skin’s surface to 1064 nm (the wavelength used in brain research). The result: red light reaches five centimeters into muscle, joint and deep tissue to promote recovery and reduce soreness.

Helio Nova helps with pain and inflammation, supports weight loss, improves brain health and kickstarts hair growth.

There are five pre-set modes: face and skin, pain and inflammation, weight loss, brain health, hair and full spectrum. It’s easy to use, with a 360-degree rotating stand, and durable thanks to 100,000-plus-hour LEDs. Store it in the corner of your living room, and whip it out whenever you need a dose of self-care; it’ll last you for years to come. The panel also has zero blue light, meaning it’s gentle on the skin and safe for the eyes.

Type: Full-body panel | Time Commitment: 10-20 minutes per session, 5 days a week | Results: 2-4 weeks of use

Whether you’re an athlete or someone who simply spends a lot of time on foot, this device gives your muscles some much-needed TLC. It delivers targeted red and near-infrared light deep into your muscles and joints to alleviate pain and expedite recovery.

This is particularly beneficial for runners who want some relief post-training without leaving the comfort of their couch. Simply place the device on your thighs, shins, arms or back to ignite cellular energy production.

Type: Cordless, wearable device | Time Commitment: 20 to 30 minutes per session | Results: 3 weeks of use

Red light therapy can actually be used to improve gum circulation and boost the overall health and freshness of your mouth. Choose from four custom modes of red (660nm) and near infrared (830nm) light during your daily brushing. It’s also great to incorporate into your routine if you’re recovering from a dental procedure.

Type: Cordless | Time Commitment: 2 minutes per session, twice a day | Results: 2-4 weeks

Sometimes, you just don’t have time to make it to the spa. So multitask instead: take care of your skin and catch up on TV while you lounge in this mask, which features enhanced eye protection. It has three times as many LED lights (360 medical-grade) as other competitive brands, ensuring full-face coverage.

It emits three different types of light — red (635nm), infrared (830nm) and blue (415nm) — that actively fight against signs of aging, reduce hyperpigmentation and crow’s feet and prevent acne.

Type: Cordless, wearable device | Time Commitment: Three to five 10-minute treatments per week | Results: 2-4 weeks

Finally — a wearable red light device designed for more than your cheekbones. The Kineon MOVE+ Pro is a modular, strap-on device built to deliver red (650nm) and near-infrared (808nm) light therapy directly to joints, tendons, and muscle groups, making it ideal for knees, shoulders, ankles, or even wrists. It’s wireless, rechargeable, and completely portable, so you can wear it during work, rest, or while plotting your revenge on whomever caused your tendinitis.

Unlike most wraparound devices that deliver weak surface light, the MOVE+ Pro uses laser diodes and LED combinations to penetrate deeper tissues and reduce inflammation where it actually starts. If you’re dealing with chronic pain, sports recovery, or even arthritis, this is a legit wearable solution, not just red light cosplay.

Type: Cordless, modular wearable device | Time Commitment: 5–15 minutes per session, once or twice daily | Results: 2–4 weeks of consistent use

Hair thinning? Scalp inflammation? Low-level laser therapy (LLLT) is one of the few scientifically backed methods to stimulate hair regrowth and improve scalp health, without relying on minoxidil or panic-buying hats. The Mito Red Light Professional Laser Therapy Helmet uses 200 diodes and a combination of red and near-infrared light to improve circulation and cellular regeneration at the follicular level.

It’s FDA-cleared, hands-free, and comfortable enough to wear while scrolling, emailing, or spiraling in silence on your couch. With consistent use (think 3 times per week, 20 minutes per session), studies show LLLT may help restore hair density and quality, especially for androgenic alopecia. You won’t see results overnight, but with patience, this helmet can quietly change the game — no greasy serums required.

Type: Cordless helmet | Time Commitment: 12-minute sessions every other day | Results: Within 3–6 months of consistent use

Wait, red light for your lips? Turns out, the LED isn’t only about its anti-aging properties. This compact device emits seven wavelengths of targeted light and offers four treatment modes that plump lips, whiten teeth, soothe gums and fight cold sores. And yes, it also helps smooth fine lines on the skin surrounding the lips and mouth.

Every order comes with a complimentary GLOwhite Teeth Whitening Gel as an extra gift.

Type: Cordless | Time Commitment: 10 minutes per session | Results: Within a few hours or days

If your primary goal is to channel your inner beached seal, the CurrentBody Skin LED Mask is a derm-favorite for a reason. This silicone mask molds to your face like a second skin and uses clinically proven red and near-infrared wavelengths to improve elasticity, smooth fine lines, and reduce redness. It’s hands-free and fits flush against the skin, which means more effective absorption and a spa-like experience without the $200 facial.

This is the mask you’ve seen all over TikTok (including on A-list celebs who pretend to be low-maintenance). It’s gentle enough for daily use, with results visible in as little as four weeks — and it doesn’t make you look like a cyborg with rage issues, which is nice.

Type: Flexible silicone face mask | Time Commitment: 10 minutes per session, 3–5 times per week | Results: Within 4 weeks

To determine the best red light therapy devices, we tested models across various formats, including masks, wands, panels, and hybrids. We evaluated ease of use, LED power output, safety certifications (FDA clearance or medical-grade classification), and effectiveness for various use cases — skin clarity, muscle soreness, inflammation, and mood.

Devices were tested over a 2-week period for consistency, comfort, visible improvements, and overall user experience. Bonus points were given for portability, battery life, and thoughtful design features like auto shut-off, timers, and accessories.

Red light therapy (RLT), also known as low-level laser therapy (LLLT) or photobiomodulation (PBM), is a non-invasive treatment that utilizes specific wavelengths of red and near-infrared light (typically between 600 and 1000 nanometers) to stimulate cellular activity. This light penetrates the skin and is absorbed by the mitochondria — the energy-producing components of cells — enhancing the production of adenosine triphosphate (ATP).

Increased ATP production can improve cellular function, promoting healing and regeneration. Clinical studies have demonstrated that RLT can aid in skin rejuvenation, reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and support hair growth. For instance, research has shown that RLT can effectively treat conditions like acne vulgaris and androgenetic alopecia, and improve skin texture and tone.

While RLT shows promise in a number of therapeutic areas, it’s important to note that its efficacy can vary depending on the condition being treated and the levels of the therapy, such as wavelength, dosage, and treatment duration. Some studies have reported benefits in muscle recovery and pain reduction, particularly in conditions like knee osteoarthritis. However, more extensive and standardized clinical trials are needed to fully establish optimal treatment protocols and long-term safety.

Additionally, while we love an at-home RLT device since they are widely available and considered safe, they may be less powerful than professional-grade equipment. And, of course, as with any therapeutic treatment, it’s advisable to consult with a healthcare professional before starting RLT to ensure it’s appropriate for your specific health needs.

Red and near-infrared light penetrates the skin and stimulates mitochondrial function to produce more adenosine triphosphate (ATP), boosting cellular regeneration and reducing inflammation. This helps improve skin tone, muscle recovery, and even mood.

Yes, red light therapy is considered safe when used as directed. Most high-quality devices are FDA-cleared and emit wavelengths that do not damage DNA or cause burns. However, protective eyewear is recommended when treating areas near the eyes.

Methylene blue can enhance mitochondrial activity and may synergize with RLT when used carefully. It acts as a redox agent and can improve the electron transport chain function when activated by light. However, consult a healthcare provider before combining the two.

Most studies suggest that 3 to 5 sessions per week, lasting 10 to 20 minutes, are beneficial for the skin. Muscle recovery may benefit from daily use, depending on intensity. Always follow manufacturer guidelines.

Larry English — a former San Diego Chargers pass rusher taken just 15 picks after Matthew Stafford in the 2009 NFL Draft — has been sued after he allegedly did not pay back a massive loan.

Debt collectors filed a lawsuit against English in Los Angeles County this month, accusing him of stiffing City National Bank out of $93,500, court documents obtained by the California Post on Tuesday show.

English, alongside his Mind Body Mastery business, entered into an agreement with the bank on Aug. 7, 2024, according to the suit.

The bank allegedly agreed to loan money to English, and in exchange, the ex-NFL player promised to pay it back, plus interest.

However, English “has failed and refused” to pay the debt, the lawsuit stated.

The debt collectors are suing English for breach of contract and are seeking $93,500 plus interest at a rate of 11.50 percent. They’re also asking for reasonable attorney’s fees.

A message seeking comment from English on Tuesday was not returned.

After being selected by the Chargers with the 16th overall pick of the 2009 NFL Draft, English struggled to live up to expectations.

The former Northern Illinois standout started just nine games in five seasons with the Bolts, only recording 11 total sacks.

He finished his career in 2014 with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, starting just one game and recording just one sack.

In retirement, English, who’s married to model Nicole Williams English, has entered into the health and wellness space, amassing 130,000 followers on Instagram.

LUJAN, Argentina, Nov. 11, (Reuters) – Pope Leo wrapped up his visit to Argentina on Wednesday with a final event drawing 2 million people, before continuing on ​his 12-day South America tour with a visit to Peru in an emotional homecoming for the first Peruvian citizen to lead the Catholic Church.

Leo, on a three-nation tour ‌through Nov. 17, celebrated an outdoor Mass at the shrine of Our Lady of Lujan, Argentina’s most important Catholic devotional site, where throngs of pilgrims gathered for days in advance for a chance to see him.

Crowds stretched for miles outside the shrine, about an hour west of Buenos Aires. People pressed against security barriers, chanting “Leo, Leo, Leo” and waving white-and-yellow Vatican flags as he arrived in an open-air popemobile.

Some in the crowd had walked as far as 10 km (six miles) to arrive, as ​many streets, including a main highway, were closed as a security measure.

In his sermon, Leo asked God to protect Argentina and urged Argentines to have a place for everyone in their society, “especially ​those who are most in need: the poor and the hungry, migrants, the sick and prisoners.”

The pope on Wednesday also visited one of Argentina’s largest ⁠penitentiaries, where he hugged several inmates and urged guards to treat detainees humanely, amid a three-day visit to Argentina that has highlighted the Church’s criticism of President Javier Milei’s cuts to social programs.

The pope, ​who has US and Peruvian citizenship, will then begin a personal leg of the most intense overseas trip by a pope in decades, returning to the place he served as a missionary for about 20 ​years before becoming pope last year.

Leo began the trip less than a month after lung cancer surgery and has appeared in good form over the intense itinerary, giving long speeches in a firm, clear voice.

The Peru visit, expected to include emotional scenes as the pope visits old friends and spends three days in the northern city of Chiclayo, where he was bishop from 2015 to 2023, will also test how directly he is willing to wade into ​the politics of his adopted nation.

Crowds for Leo’s visit to Argentina have been intense, with the pope drawing more than 6 million people across his visit. A Mass in Buenos Aires on Monday ​was the largest single event yet of his 18-month papacy, drawing 2.5 million.

Leo is due to land at Peru’s Callao Air Base at 5:30 p.m. (2230 GMT). After a brief welcome ceremony, he ‌will head ⁠to the presidential palace for a closely watched address to President Keiko Fujimori, who was elected this year in one of Peru’s closest elections, marred by fraud accusations and vote-counting delays.

Fujimori is the daughter of former President Alberto Fujimori, who was in office from 1990 to 2000 and died in 2024. Her victory marked the return of one of Peru’s most influential and polarizing political dynasties.

In 2017, Leo, then known as Bishop Robert Prevost, criticized the late Fujimori’s pardon. He said the former president, who had been convicted of serious human rights abuses, should personally seek forgiveness from victims if Peru was to achieve ​genuine reconciliation.

Keiko Fujimori leaned heavily on her father’s political ​legacy during her presidential campaign.

“It’s not just ⁠a pastoral visit by the pope to his flock, but a visit to his home,” said Jose Luis Guadalupe Pérez, an academic at Peru’s Pacific University. Leo’s intimate knowledge of Peru, he added, means “he is bound to step on some toes.”

Peru has prepared for the homecoming with fervor: a 14-meter (46-foot) statue depicting ​Leo with outstretched arms towers over a seaside park in Callao, merchants in Lima sell pope-themed shirts and souvenirs, and inmates at the country’s ​largest women’s prison have stitched velvet ⁠dolls bearing his likeness.

The Peru leg caps Leo’s first tour of South America as pope, where he has appealed for political dialogue and greater unity across a divided region.

Martin Cassinelli, an analyst at the Atlantic Council, said Leo’s Peruvian roots give him an unusual ability to speak about the country’s political past.

“There’s no other country where the Pope is as attuned to the domestic politics of that country than Peru,” ⁠Cassinelli said.

“If there’s ​anything that could potentially be at odds with the current Fujimori government, it would be a reflection on the past.”

Relations ​between the late Fujimori’s government and sectors of the Catholic Church were frequently tense, particularly over human rights during the state’s fight against the Maoist Shining Path insurgency.

Church figures also opposed the 1995 amnesty for members of the security forces ​accused of rights abuses.

Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s new neighbors are already predicting trouble in paradise.

The couple’s landscaping plans for their $5.35 million Bratenahl, Ohio, estate sparked a heated debate at a local town meeting, with one disgruntled resident brutally predicting the pair would be broken up within a decade.

“To be perfectly honest, I think it’s all stupid. It’s all subjective,” one neighbor declared during the Architectural Review Board meeting at the Bratenahl Community Center on Tuesday.

He continued, “This effort that’s being put in for Taylor Swift, I think for a property that’s pretty much going to be a timeshare and sold in seven to 10 years when the divorce happens, I think it’s ridiculous.”

The bitter remark prompted a chorus of boos from the crowd of 35 attendees.

“That’s fine, it’s just a different opinion,” the man fired back.

Another neighbor, who is a frequent attendee at village meetings, shared that he took issue with Kelce and Swift’s plans to plant 10-foot shrubs outside the residence for privacy measures.

“I live two houses away from the property in question and I do have complaints,” Chuck Bauernschmidt said. “This is not going to be open. This is a forest, and I’m not sure why the board is going in that direction. You’re going against ordinances? Am I mistaken? I don’t think I am. I feel bad for the village.”

Another neighbor who lives three doors down from the home voiced concern for how the landscaping plans will impact wildlife.

“Here is a wonderful opportunity for people who have money to put it into the caliber that this house should have,” Lucy Weller said.

“I think this is a wonderful opportunity for this camp to go back and learn a bit about native species and designs that show off what animals need in this area.

“They don’t need lawns; they need food and cover and they need places to have sex. I don’t think this landscape does anything to provide for any of the wildlife.”

Several locals jumped to their defense, arguing that the athlete and Grammy winner should be welcomed by the community.

“We should feel privileged that these people chose this location for their residence and instead we are arguing over landscape and privacy as opposed to coming together as a community and looking at it as, wow, they chose Bratenahl, because Bratenahl is a special place,” Vasiliki Diamantis said.

“We should accept them regardless of how many days they live here.”

Diamantis was met with applause, and another neighbor agreed, telling the crowd, “I have to mirror that.”

“I think it would be an absolute sin if this community goes in any way other than supporting people who are coming to our lovely neighborhood,” the man, a lawyer, said. “It would be a shame. I think we should support these people and welcome them with open arms.”

Despite the back-and-forth, the board unanimously approved the plans, which include updated brickwork and a mix of staggered deciduous shrubs that will reach a maximum height of 10 feet when fully grown.

Swift and Kelce did not attend the meeting. Instead, they were represented by house manager Patrick Hyland, landscape architect Derek Kuryla and Jacob Kutz of Tiny Construction.

As Page Six previously reported, the duo, who tied the knot in July, purchased the eight-bedroom, 11-bathroom historic mansion in March.

In September, they received approval to erect a six-foot black aluminum privacy fence around portions of the property, despite objections from nearby homeowners. That same month, Page Six exclusively reported that Swift and Kelce were taking extreme security measures at the Ohio home.

We previously reported that the pop star, 36, and Kansas City Chiefs tight end, 37, won’t be using the mansion as their primary home.

Swift already maintains an impressive real estate portfolio, with homes in Rhode Island, Beverly Hills, Nashville and New York City.

Page Six has reached out to reps for Swift and Kelce for comment.

So they are extremely active in talks.

But can they actually do anything significant yet? That seems to be a major question.

Some in fact are suggesting the Yankees are one of a number of teams in a virtual holding pattern until the rules for 2027 and beyond are set. Meantime, general manager Brian Cashman told The Post, flat out, “I have not been told that.”

Later, in the full media session, Cashman repeated the phrase “business as usual” several times to describe how he’s handling these GM meetings in this unusual offseason with a lockout coming Dec. 1 that’s going to shut down the sport. And by all accounts he is operating exactly as he would in a more normal offseason — talking to agents and other GMs about signings and trades, working the Aria hotel and gathering info so that he can pounce on opportunities.

پوشش خبری بیشتر ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود ببینید. لاس وگاس — یانکی‌ها درباره بازیکن مطرح رنجرز، کوری سیگر، شورت‌استاپ، مذاکره کرده‌اند، بازار بازیکنان دوم‌بیس را که شامل بازیکنان آزاد مطرحی مانند براندون لو و لوئیس آراه‌س می‌شود، بررسی کرده‌اند، به دنبال بازیکنان پست کچر راست‌دست، از جمله کارسون کلی بوده‌اند که می‌تواند با آستین ولز زوج شود، و بدون شک درباره کمک در پست بولپن سؤال کرده‌اند. بنابراین آنها در مذاکرات بسیار فعال هستند. اما آیا واقعاً هنوز می‌توانند کار مهمی انجام دهند؟ به نظر می‌رسد این یک سؤال مهم باشد. پیام‌های متنی گرگ جویس از برانکس و فراتر از آن را از دست ندهید — او به مشترکین Sports+ اطلاعات داخلی درباره یانکی‌ها می‌دهد. در واقع برخی معتقدند که یانکی‌ها یکی از چندین تیمی هستند که تا زمانی که قوانین برای سال 2027 و بعد از آن تعیین نشود، عملاً در حالت تعلیق قرار دارند. در همین حال، برایان کشمن، مدیرعامل، صراحتاً به The Post گفت: «چنین چیزی به من گفته نشده است. ”
بعداً، در جلسه کامل با رسانه‌ها، کشمن چندین بار عبارت «همه چیز مثل همیشه» را تکرار کرد تا توصیف کند که چگونه در این فصل نقل و انتقالات غیرمعمول با اعتصاب کاری که از 1 دسامبر آغاز می‌شود و باعث توقف این ورزش خواهد شد، این جلسات مدیران باشگاه را مدیریت می‌کند. و از هر نظر دقیقاً همان کاری را انجام می‌دهد که در یک فصل نقل و انتقالات عادی انجام می‌داد — با مدیربرنامه‌ها و سایر مدیران عامل درباره قراردادها و معامله‌ها صحبت می‌کند، در هتل آریا کار می‌کند و اطلاعات جمع‌آوری می‌کند تا بتواند از فرصت‌ها استفاده کند.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

A scientific breakthrough underscores what my cat-fanatic editor has long believed: humans are essentially simps for their cats.

Researchers from the University of São Paulo in Brazil have found that a cat’s meow is essentially a demand that we, their mortal lessers, solve their problem.

To prove the point, scientists introduced an “unsolvable task” to 38 domestic cats to assess what happened when their simp solvers were present versus nowhere in sight.

Shockingly, the nonplussed felines were four times more likely to get vocal when a human was there to hear them.

“These results are consistent with meowing playing a communicative role in cat-human interactions,” the study authors wrote in a paper published in Animal Behaviour.

It’s well established that cats meow frequently and at great volume when their humans are around and are decidedly mum in their own company.

Further, feral cats meow at a much lower rate than their domesticated brethren, indicating that the sound is at least partially influenced by the presence of human beings.

Earlier research found that the sounds domesticated cats make have evolved over time to make the tone more coercive to humans.

“Short, higher-pitched sounds are more pleasing to our auditory system, because young humans have high-pitched voices, so cats have evolved to curry our favor,” Jonathan Losos writes in “The Cat’s Meow: How Cats Evolved From the Savanna to Your Sofa.”

Over thousands of years of cohabitation, their purrs have also evolved to sound “nicer” to our ears.

However, it is the meow, specifically, that seems designed to make us do their bidding, with different pitches that loosely translate to “feed me, you knave;” “permit me royal entry through this blocked portal, worm;” and “you are sanctioned to pet me, plebe.”

In this latest round of research, Naila Fukimoto of the University of São Paulo and her team recruited 38 feline familiars who had a history of meowing for and around food.

Each feline participant was faced with — and tortured by — “an unsolvable task”: A snack trapped inside a small plastic box punctured with holes.

The cats could smell and see the treat but lacked the requisite opposable thumbs to access it.

Researchers observed how the cats reacted after one minute when no human was present versus when a human was in the room.

If a human was there to hear them, the cats got vocal; researchers recorded 85 meows compared to just 20 when the cat was alone.

Statistical analysis showed that cats were 16 times more likely to meow when a human was around.

“During an unsolvable task involving their favorite food item, cats produced significantly more meows when a human was present compared to when they were alone, which is consistent with meowing functioning as a socially directed signal,” the study authors wrote.

In addition to amplifying their pleas, cats in the company of humans gazed imploringly toward their minions. They shifted their heads between the humans and the snack box, clearly instructing them to solve the problem.

Conversely, when the cats were alone, they spent a majority of their time staring at the door, presumably summoning their human to help.

These behaviors indicate that the cats were not simply rallying against the injustice of a captive snack but modifying their behavior in the presence of someone who could help.

Researchers underscore that this doesn’t prove cats consciously view humans as problem solvers or calculate every vocalization to manipulate them. Still, it does indicate that meowing is much more purposeful than an emotional reflex.

“The recipient-directed nature of the majority of meows recorded in our study indicates that cats were not simply vocalizing into the environment but targeting a specific audience, consistent with recipient-specific signaling,” the researchers concluded.

The team noted some limitations, namely that the subject pool was small and that they deliberately highlighted cats with a history of food vocalization.
news.content:
بیشتر پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. یک پیشرفت علمی بر آن چیزی تأکید می کند که ویراستار متعصب گربه من برای مدت طولانی به آن اعتقاد داشته است: انسان ها اساساً برای گربه های خود ساده هستند. محققان دانشگاه سائوپائولو در برزیل دریافته اند که میو گربه اساساً خواسته ای است که ما، کوچکترهای فانی آنها، مشکل آنها را حل کنیم. برای اثبات این موضوع، دانشمندان یک «وظیفه غیرقابل حل» را به 38 گربه خانگی معرفی کردند تا ارزیابی کنند که چه اتفاقی افتاده است وقتی که حل‌کننده‌های ساده آن‌ها حضور داشتند در مقابل هیچ جایی. در رفتار حیوانات به خوبی ثابت شده است که گربه‌ها زمانی که انسان‌هایشان در اطراف هستند، اغلب و با صدای زیاد می‌میو می‌کنند و به طور قطعی در شرکت خودشان مادر هستند. علاوه بر این، گربه‌های وحشی با سرعت بسیار کمتری نسبت به برادران اهلی‌شان می‌میو می‌کنند و این نشان می‌دهد که صدا حداقل تا حدی تحت‌تاثیر حضور انسان‌ها قرار دارد. تحقیقات قبلی نشان می‌دهد که صداهای اهلی‌شده به گربه‌ها را در طول زمان بیشتر کرده است. جاناتان لوسوس در «میو گربه: چگونه گربه ها از ساوانا به مبل شما تکامل یافتند» می نویسد: «صداهای کوتاه و بلندتر برای سیستم شنوایی ما خوشایندتر است، زیرا انسان های جوان صدای بلندی دارند، بنابراین گربه ها تکامل یافته اند تا ما را جلب کنند.»
بیش از هزار

news.originalContent:
Moscow announces the veteran diplomat’s sudden passing without further details.

Russia’s ambassador to the United States, Alexander Darchiev, has died at the age of 66, according to the Russian Foreign Ministry.

The ministry said in a statement that he “passed away suddenly” on Wednesday, just a year and a half after being appointed to the US role.

Moscow did not provide more details on his death.

Darchiev was an “outstanding diplomat, an experienced leader and a kind colleague” and worked “in one of the most critical areas of Russian foreign policy”, the ministry said. He was a specialist in Russia-US relations.

He was appointed last March, shortly after US President Donald Trump returned to power, and several years into Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

In 2022, when Russia launched its offensive against Ukraine, Darchiev called the move a “necessary measure”.

Darchiev was born into the family of a diplomat and minister-counsellor of the Russian Embassy in Hungary, Nikita Ivanovich Darchiev, according to the state-owned TASS news agency.

He first entered diplomatic service in 1992, becoming first secretary and head of the North America department in Russia’s Foreign Ministry.

He served as an adviser to the Russian Embassy in the US in 1997 and later took the post of minister-counsellor from 2005 to 2010. He also previously served as Russia’s ambassador to Canada between 2014 and 2021.

Darchiev returned to the North America department in the Foreign Ministry as its director in 2010 and later held the post again until last year.
news.content: مسکو مرگ ناگهانی این دیپلمات کهنه کار را بدون جزئیات بیشتر اعلام می کند. به گفته وزارت امور خارجه روسیه، الکساندر دارچیف، سفیر روسیه در ایالات متحده در سن 66 سالگی درگذشت. این وزارتخانه در بیانیه ای اعلام کرد که وی روز چهارشنبه، تنها یک سال و نیم پس از انتصاب به سمت آمریکا، "به طور ناگهانی درگذشت." وزارت امور خارجه روسیه گفت که دارچیف یک "دیپلمات برجسته، یک رهبر با تجربه و یک همکار مهربان" بود و "در یکی از حیاتی ترین حوزه های سیاست خارجی روسیه" کار می کرد. او متخصص روابط روسیه و ایالات متحده بود. او در مارس گذشته، اندکی پس از بازگشت دونالد ترامپ، رئیس جمهور ایالات متحده به قدرت، و چندین سال پس از تهاجم تمام عیار مسکو به اوکراین، منصوب شد. در سال 2022، زمانی که روسیه حمله خود را علیه اوکراین آغاز کرد، دارچیف این اقدام را "اقدام ضروری" خواند. به گزارش خبرگزاری دولتی TASS، دارچیف در خانواده یک دیپلمات و وزیر مشاور سفارت روسیه در مجارستان، نیکیتا ایوانوویچ دارچیف، متولد شد. او برای اولین بار در سال 1992 به عنوان رئیس وزارت امور خارجه روسیه وارد خدمت دیپلماتیک شد و در سال 1992 به عنوان اولین رئیس وزارت امور خارجه روسیه در وزارت امور خارجه شرکت کرد. او در سال 1997 به عنوان مشاور سفارت روسیه در ایالات متحده خدمت کرد و پس از آن از سال 2005 تا 2010 سمت وزیر مشاور را بر عهده گرفت. او همچنین قبلاً به عنوان سفیر روسیه در کانادا بین سال های 2014 تا 2021 خدمت کرده بود. دارچیف به بخش آمریکای شمالی در وزارت خارجه بازگشت.

news.originalContent:
Authorities spared no effort in preparation for the Atlantic storm after criticism following January’s Storm Kristin.

More than 300 flights in and out of Portugal have been cancelled, while businesses and all schools nationwide shut down before Storm Charles hit the country’s mainland, but the heavy rainfall and intense winds passed without causing severe damage.

Operations shut down on Wednesday across four different international airports, as well as hundreds of supermarkets and all non-essential public services across the country.

For the first time in living memory, about 8,000 of Portugal’s schools cancelled classes over the significant Atlantic storm forecast.

Streets were largely deserted when Storm Charles arrived, because the government had told people to stay at home, fearing the worst.

The national weather agency, IPMA, recorded wind gusts of more than 120km/h (75mph) in some areas.

Buses without passengers drove through the country’s capital, Lisbon, where some streets flooded due to clogged drains.

A national supermarket chain closed its stores, while the Web Summit technology conference in Lisbon, attended by about 70,000 people, called off the day’s events.

By mid-afternoon, only the southern Algarve region, a popular European tourist destination, remained on red alert, the highest level of emergency warning, which initially had covered more than half of the country.

Storm Charles had struck the Portuguese island of Madeira, off northwest Africa, on Tuesday with 130km/h (81mph) winds.

In January, the country’s centre-right government faced harsh criticism for its weak response when Storm Kristin hit central Portugal, felling thousands of trees and causing widespread property damage that is still being repaired.

In February, a 70-year-old man died in the southern region of Alentejo after flooding swept his vehicle off a street in the aftermath of Storm Leonardo.

Prime Minister Luis Montenegro chaired a crisis unit along with eight government ministers and other officials to monitor the storm.

Interior Minister Luis Neves, who oversees public safety, dismissed suggestions that authorities had overreacted, saying the government organised its response in accordance with the weather forecast.

Storm Charles was forecast to head later into Spain, where workers staged a general strike Wednesday. Strike organisers cancelled or postponed demonstrations in some southern cities, including Cordoba, Huelva and Cadiz.
news.content: مقامات هیچ تلاشی را برای آمادگی در برابر طوفان اقیانوس اطلس پس از انتقاداتی که به دنبال طوفان کریستین در ژانویه مطرح شد، دریغ نکردند. بیش از 300 پرواز ورودی و خروجی پرتغال لغو شد، در حالی که مشاغل و همه مدارس در سراسر کشور قبل از اینکه طوفان چارلز به سرزمین اصلی این کشور برسد، تعطیل شدند، اما بارندگی شدید و بادهای شدید بدون ایجاد خسارت شدید سپری شد. روز چهارشنبه فعالیت‌ها در چهار فرودگاه بین‌المللی مختلف و همچنین صدها سوپرمارکت و تمام خدمات عمومی غیرضروری در سراسر کشور متوقف شد. برای اولین بار در تاریخ معاصر، حدود 8000 مدرسه در پرتغال به دلیل پیش‌بینی طوفان شدید اقیانوس اطلس، کلاس‌ها را لغو کردند. زمانی که طوفان چارلز رسید، خیابان‌ها تقریباً خالی از جمعیت بودند، زیرا دولت به مردم گفته بود که به دلیل ترس از وقوع بدترین شرایط، در خانه‌های خود بمانند. سازمان ملی هواشناسی، IPMA، وزش بادهای شدید با سرعت بیش از 120 کیلومتر بر ساعت (75 مایل بر ساعت) را در برخی مناطق ثبت کرد. اتوبوس‌های بدون مسافر در پایتخت کشور، لیسبون، تردد می‌کردند که در آن برخی خیابان‌ها به دلیل گرفتگی فاضلاب‌ها دچار سیلاب شدند. یک زنجیره سوپرمارکت ملی فروشگاه‌های خود را تعطیل کرد، در حالی که کنفرانس فناوری Web Summit در لیسبون که حدود 70,000 نفر در آن شرکت داشتند، برنامه‌های آن روز را لغو کرد. تا اواسط بعدازظهر، تنها منطقه جنوبی آلگاروه، یک مقصد گردشگری محبوب اروپایی، در حالت هشدار قرمز، بالاترین سطح هشدار اضطراری، باقی ماند که در ابتدا بیش از نیمی از کشور را تحت تأثیر قرار داده بود. طوفان چارلز روز سه‌شنبه به جزیره مادیرا در پرتغال، در شمال غربی آفریقا، برخورد کرد.

news.originalContent:
Lawmakers have pledged to use new majorities in House and Senate to pursue the investigation into Epstein’s network.

One of the key issues Democrats brought up against the Trump administration and the Republican Party in this month’s midterm elections was how they had handled the investigation into convicted sex trafficker Jeffrey Epstein.

United States President Donald Trump had pledged to release troves of files on Epstein gathered by the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and other federal agencies when he was campaigning for president in 2024.

But after taking office, Trump administration officials were accused of thwarting efforts to bring transparency to the issue, and Trump himself publicly rebuked the handful of Republican lawmakers who sided with Democrats to force declassification of what federal investigators had uncovered over the years. Some of those lawmakers even lost their seats after Trump withdrew his support and backed primary opponents.

Now, Democratic lawmakers, who will control a majority in both the House and Senate beginning in January, say they plan to use legislative powers to confront the Trump administration on Epstein. As the majority party, Democrats can appoint lawmakers to lead key committees that have the power to issue subpoenas to officials and hold hearings where those officials could be asked to answer questions under oath about the handling of the files.

Although Trump could still use his veto power to overrule legislation Democrats might pass, for instance, to mandate further disclosures from the administration, the committees they control will wield considerable investigative power that was previously not exercised by Republicans.

On Tuesday, the currently Republican-controlled House Oversight Committee issued findings (PDF) from a 15-month investigation into the federal government’s role in the Epstein investigation. The committee called for specific steps for the Department of Justice to take, including interviewing and re-interviewing key witnesses, and further investigating Epstein’s network of associates.

The committee stopped short of calling for investigating any links Trump might have had with Epstein, something Democratic lawmakers have called for. Instead, the current committee’s report said Democrats on the body were “obsessed with trying to implicate President Trump” and engaged in an “unfounded witch hunt”. The Republican-led body said it “did not identify any documents that would implicate President Trump in any criminal activity related to Epstein and Maxwell”.

Incoming Democratic lawmakers expected to chair the House Oversight Committee, as well as the Senate Finance Committee, are already saying they plan to use their powers to demand more answers from the Trump administration.

In November 2025, lawmakers passed the Epstein Files Transparency Act, in a notably bipartisan fashion: just one member of the House voted against the law, and no one in the Senate opposed it.

The law called on the Justice Department to release “all unclassified records, documents, communications and investigative materials” it had related to the Epstein investigation and prosecution of the sex offender. Those documents also had to be made available in “a searchable and downloadable format”.

Millions of documents were eventually released, but many were heavily redacted, and lawmakers who had access to the unredacted versions said some of that information deserved to be public, and more files were in the possession of the Trump administration.

Democrats on some committees have already been involved in the Epstein investigation in some way, and even as minority members, some have been able to issue reports to at least call for more inquiries.

In October, Democrats on the House Judiciary Committee released a 53-page report (PDF) specifically looking into ties between Trump and Epstein. Trump has denied having any serious contact with Epstein, and said he had no part in the convicted sex-trafficker’s activities.

Democrats say they based their report on publicly available information, as well as interviews with women who they say were abused by Epstein and Trump. Five women, the report claims, accused Trump of “rape or sexual assault in Epstein’s company or presence”.

Trump has denied those allegations.

The report also claims the FBI was told by one witness that Trump was introduced to his wife Melania Trump by Epstein and that the president was involved in Epstein’s sex-trafficking network. It also claims Attorney General Todd Blanche instructed Epstein’s associate Ghislaine Maxwell not to speak about ties between the sex trafficker and Trump. Blanche has denied doing so.

Democratic Representative Robert Garcia, who is expected to take over as chair of the House Oversight Committee, has said he intends to pursue officials like Blanche and others as part of his investigation. The committee, which acts as a watchdog, has a broad mandate to look into the work of federal agencies, like the Justice Department.

Garcia said this week on US television network MS NOW that he plans to use subpoena powers to force Blanche to answer questions. “He doesn’t want to answer questions, because he’s scared, because he knows that he’s been involved in leading this White House coverup related to the Epstein files,” Garcia said.

On Tuesday, the currently Republican-led House Oversight Committee, which is led by Republicans, called on federal authorities to review whether banks failed to properly deal with suspicious transactions involving Epstein.

One committee in the Senate that is likely to take action is the Finance Committee, whose expected chair, Democratic Senator Ron Wyden, has said he plans to follow up on findings in his own report on the Epstein scandal.

In August, Wyden’s office issued a 67-page report (PDF) on how major banks in the US and the US Department of the Treasury allegedly failed to act on suspicious transactions by Epstein and his associates, who moved money around the globe as part of their trafficking network.

“Wall Street banks enabled Epstein for years. By failing to report—or choosing not to report—his suspicious financial transactions to federal law enforcement, these banks allowed Epstein to send cash payments and wire transfers to his victims, friends, and collaborators around the world,” the report found.

Major banks including JPMorgan Chase, Deutsche Bank, and Bank of America, Wyden’s report claims, moved more than $1bn around for Epstein and his network in thousands of transactions over the years that should have been reported as possible criminal activity.

“I have a list of Wall Street bankers who need to answer questions about why they looked the other way while Epstein and his cronies sent millions of dollars through their institutions to facilitate sex trafficking women and girls,” Wyden said in a statement last week. “As Finance Committee chair, every tool will be on the table to get answers.”
news.content: قانونگذاران متعهد شده اند که از اکثریت های جدید مجلس نمایندگان و سنا برای پیگیری تحقیقات در مورد شبکه اپستین استفاده کنند. یکی از موضوعات کلیدی که دموکرات ها علیه دولت ترامپ و حزب جمهوری خواه در انتخابات میان دوره ای این ماه مطرح کردند، نحوه رسیدگی آنها به تحقیقات درباره قاچاقچی جنسی محکوم به جنایت جفری اپستین بود. دونالد ترامپ، رئیس‌جمهور ایالات متحده، متعهد شده بود که مجموعه‌ای از پرونده‌های مربوط به اپشتین را که توسط اداره تحقیقات فدرال (اف‌بی‌آی) و دیگر آژانس‌های فدرال جمع‌آوری شده بود، در زمان مبارزات انتخاباتی اپشتین برای ریاست‌جمهوری در سال 2024 منتشر کند. اما پس از روی کار آمدن، مقامات دولت ترامپ متهم شدند که تلاش‌ها برای شفاف‌سازی این موضوع را خنثی می‌کنند و خود ترامپ علناً تعداد انگشت شماری از قانون‌گذاران جمهوری‌خواه را که در کنار دموکرات‌ها قرار گرفتند تا آنچه را که بازرسان فدرال طی سال‌ها کشف کرده بودند، از حالت طبقه‌بندی خارج کنند، سرزنش کرد. برخی از این قانونگذاران حتی پس از اینکه ترامپ از حمایت خود عقب نشینی کرد و از مخالفان اولیه حمایت کرد، کرسی های خود را از دست دادند. اکنون، قانونگذاران دموکرات که از ماه ژانویه اکثریت مجلس و سنا را در دست خواهند داشت، می گویند که قصد دارند از اختیارات قانونگذاری برای مقابله با دولت ترامپ در مورد اپشتین استفاده کنند. به عنوان حزب اکثریت، دموکرات‌ها می‌توانند قانون‌گذاران را برای رهبری کمیته‌های کلیدی که قدرت صدور احضاریه برای مقامات را دارند و جلسات استماع برگزار می‌کنند که در آن مقامات می‌توانند تحت سوگند در مورد رسیدگی به پرونده‌ها به سوالات پاسخ دهند، منصوب کنند. اگرچه ترامپ همچنان می تواند از حق وتوی خود برای رد قوانین دموکراسی استفاده کند

news.originalContent:
Democratic Colorado state Sen. Iman Jodeh, the state’s first Muslim lawmaker, announced a paid internship at the state capitol with qualifications requiring that candidates identify as Muslim or descend from predominantly Muslim regions of the world.

Jodeh posted the notice of the Legislative Intern Program and its qualifications Monday, less than a week after securing her seat in the midterm election. (RELATED: MLB Team Speaks Out After Player Posts Video Of Christian Preacher Trashing Islam)

“Gain first-hand experience at the Colorado Capitol in Sen. Jodeh and Rep. Zokaie’s offices!” the digital flyer said, adding that qualified candidates would receive a $1,000 stipend.

Along with qualifications expected for such a role, such as being an undergraduate student with a minimum 3.5 GPA and being flexible enough to work a part-time job during the 2027 legislative session, the first credentials listed are that the candidate must “Identify as a Muslim and/or as Middle Eastern, North African, or South Asian.”

Issued under the Middle Eastern, North African, South Asian (MENASA) & Muslim Joint Legislative Caucus, the flyer raised questions over state and federal anti-discrimination statutes governing public offices and paid positions.

Colorado State Senator Iman Jodeh, who’s celebrated as the first muslim elected to the Colorado legislature, is advertising an internship program at the Colorado Capitol Qualifications are you have to be muslim or north african. This is illegal. Cc @CivilRights https://t.co/GQTGxSk1Iq

“This is illegal,” Libs of TikTok shared Wednesday, echoing many comments under Jodeh’s advertisement on Instagram.

Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 prohibits hiring or firing based on national origin and religion, among other immutable characteristics. Colorado state law also prohibits discrimination against employees based on protected classes such as religion and national origin.

While similar lawmakers and private groups often work around this by inserting “interest in” or “commitment to” clauses, the MENASA & Muslim Joint Legislative Caucus listed the identity of a specific religion or ethnicity as the first qualification for a paid internship.

Jodeh, the Department of Justice Civil Rights Division, and the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) did not respond to the Daily Caller’s request for comment by the time of publication.
news.content:
ایمان جوده، سناتور دموکرات ایالت کلرادو، اولین قانونگذار مسلمان این ایالت، یک دوره کارآموزی با حقوق در مرکز ایالت را با شرایطی که مستلزم آن است که نامزدها مسلمان باشند یا از مناطق عمدتا مسلمان نشین جهان باشند، اعلام کرد. جوده اطلاعیه برنامه کارآموزی قانونگذاری و شرایط آن را در روز دوشنبه، کمتر از یک هفته منتهی به انتخابات، پست کرد. (مرتبط: تیم MLB بعد از پست های بازیکن ویدیویی از واعظ مسیحی که اسلام را به باد می دهد صحبت می کند)
"تجربه دست اول را در کاپیتول کلرادو در دفاتر سن جوده و نماینده زوکایی به دست آورید!" بروشور دیجیتال گفت و افزود که نامزدهای واجد شرایط 1000 دلار کمک هزینه دریافت خواهند کرد. همراه با مدارک مورد انتظار برای چنین نقشی، مانند دانشجو بودن در مقطع کارشناسی با حداقل 3. 5 معدل و انعطاف پذیری کافی برای کار پاره وقت در جلسه قانونگذاری 2027، اولین مدارک ذکر شده این است که نامزد باید «مسلمان و/یا خاورمیانه، شمال آفریقا یا جنوب آسیا باشد». این اعلامیه که تحت انجمن قانونگذاری مشترک خاورمیانه، آفریقای شمالی، آسیای جنوبی (MENASA) و مسلمانان صادر شد، سوالاتی را در مورد قوانین ضد تبعیض ایالتی و فدرال حاکم بر ادارات دولتی و مناصب پولی ایجاد کرد. ایمان جوده، سناتور ایالت کلرادو، که به عنوان اولین مسلمان منتخب مجلس کلرادو شناخته می شود، در حال تبلیغ یک برنامه کارآموزی در کاپیتول کلرادو است. این غیرقانونی است. سی

news.originalContent:
Polish PM Donald Tusk calls for restraint, urging unity after deadly Krakow attack linked to far-right ideology.

Tens of thousands of nationalist sympathisers have gathered in Poland’s capital, Warsaw, for an Independence Day march, days after a mass shooting in Krakow killed six people.

Participants carrying Polish flags assembled in central Warsaw on Wednesday, as police officers were deployed at the scene to secure the demonstration.

The Independence Day march, which has long been a source of tension between right-wing groups and Poland’s governing centrists, has been held annually on November 11 since 1918 to commemorate the end of more than 100 years of partition by Russia, Prussia and Austria.

The annual march has faced criticism for anti-Semitic and anti-immigration rhetoric, while supporters say the gathering, held under the motto “A Pole is the host in Poland”, is an expression of national pride.

Organisers of the march said they expected a record turnout, with many foreign nationalists set to attend, including Spain’s Revuelta, a youth movement linked to Vox, and members of the Hungarian far-right Mi Hazank party.

Poland’s conservative-nationalist President Karol Nawrocki was seen attending the march and has previously participated in both his official capacity and as a private citizen.

Poland “does not exist today so that the political elites can grant themselves the right to manage citizens … against the will of the nation”, Nawrocki said, alluding to the centrist government.

Prior to the march, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk appealed for restraint amid heightened political divisions after ministers said the man who killed six people and wounded more than a dozen in the main square of Krakow on Saturday, November 7 may have been motivated by ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌far-right ideology.

“We may hold different views, we may keep each other in check, and at times we may even be political opponents,” Tusk said. “Anyone who truly cares about Poland must understand that this space, defined by independence, freedom and a secure Republic, is a common good.”

On Tuesday, Justice Minister Waldemar Zurek said the killer had been interested in the neo-Nazi Anders Behring Breivik, who killed 77 people in Norway in 2011.

On Monday, the police announced that the 24-year-old gunman died at a hospital after he was shot by police officers and arrested on Saturday when he opened fire from his car.
news.content: دونالد تاسک، نخست‌وزیر لهستان، پس از حمله مرگبار در کراکوف که به ایدئولوژی راست‌افراطی مرتبط بود، خواستار خویشتن‌داری و اتحاد شد. ده‌ها هزار نفر از طرفداران ملی‌گرا در پایتخت لهستان، ورشو، برای راهپیمایی روز استقلال، چند روز پس از تیراندازی گسترده در کراکوف که منجر به کشته شدن شش نفر شد، گرد هم آمدند. شرکت‌کنندگان با در دست داشتن پرچم‌های لهستان روز چهارشنبه در مرکز ورشو جمع شدند، در حالی که مأموران پلیس برای تأمین امنیت تظاهرات در محل مستقر شده بودند. راهپیمایی روز استقلال که مدت‌ها منبع تنش بین گروه‌های راست‌گرا و میانه‌روهای حاکم لهستان بوده است، از سال 1918 هر ساله در 11 نوامبر برای بزرگداشت پایان بیش از 100 سال تقسیم لهستان توسط روسیه، پروس و اتریش برگزار می‌شود. این راهپیمایی سالانه به دلیل شعارهای ضد یهود و ضد مهاجرت با انتقاداتی مواجه شده است، در حالی که حامیان آن می‌گویند این تجمع که با شعار «لهستانی‌ها میزبان لهستان هستند» برگزار می‌شود، بیانگر غرور ملی است. برگزارکنندگان راهپیمایی گفتند که انتظار دارند شاهد حضور بی‌سابقه شرکت‌کنندگان باشند، از جمله بسیاری از ملی‌گرایان خارجی که قرار است در این راهپیمایی شرکت کنند، از جمله Revuelta اسپانیا، جنبش جوانی که به Vox مرتبط است، و اعضای حزب راست‌گرای افراطی Mi Hazank مجارستان. کارول ناوروتسکی، رئیس‌جمهور محافظه‌کار-ناسیونالیست لهستان، در این راهپیمایی شرکت کرد و قبلاً نیز هم به عنوان یک مقام رسمی و هم به عنوان یک شهروند عادی در آن شرکت کرده بود. ناوروتسکی با اشاره به این موضوع گفت: «لهستان امروز وجود ندارد تا نخبگان سیاسی بتوانند حق مدیریت شهروندان را ... برخلاف خواست ملت برای خود قائل شوند.»

news.originalContent:
The Republican ran unopposed, despite some GOP lawmaker demands to evaluate the party’s stinging midterm losses to Democrats.

As they prepare to lose power, Republicans in the United States Senate have re-elected John Thune to lead their party during the final years of Donald Trump’s presidency.

At a closed-door meeting at the US Capitol on Tuesday, the South Dakota lawmaker won the support of his fellow Senate Republicans – even as some had hoped to delay the leadership vote to examine what went wrong in last week’s election.

“I appreciated the opportunity to have an open, honest, and transparent conversation with my colleagues today”, Thune said in a statement after the vote. “I am honored to have their continued trust and support to lead the Senate Republican Conference in the 120th Congress.”

Unlike two years ago, when he competed against two of his fellow Republicans to replace outgoing Senator Mitch McConnell as the party’s Senate leader, Thune ran unopposed on Tuesday for the role.

Senator Josh Hawley told reporters after the vote that “maybe there would be” a challenger if Senate Republicans had waited longer.

“I just think that we’ve got a lot of things that we’ve got to think through, and I think that to just rush into this and just ratify all of the same leadership, what message does that send?” the Missouri Republican said.

Republican Senator Ron Johnson, who circulated a letter asking for a delay in the vote, said he tried to postpone the leadership decision. He said his conference needed to do some “real soul searching” but, like Hawley, conceded that no one else had stepped up to challenge Thune.

“That’s part of our problem, who would want the job?” he said as he turned to a reporter and joked, “Do you want it?”

Thune’s re-election comes as Republicans in the US House selected Speaker Mike Johnson’s successor. Congressman Jim Jordan was elected as the US House minority leader, marking his first foray into Republican leadership.

Under Thune’s tenure, US Republicans lost at least seven Senate seats in the country’s pivotal midterms. Two US Senate races – Alaska and Mississippi – still remain uncalled.

Despite those losses, some in the party, like Senator Jim Lankford of Oklahoma, said that there is “widespread support” among Republican senators for Thune, who has taken a markedly different approach than McConnell to seek out differing viewpoints before making major decisions.

“It’s a pretty complicated role to be able to manage,” Lankford said of Thune’s role. “No one wants that job”.

Some conservative voices have attributed the party’s losses to Thune’s effort to pass the SAVE America Act, which would have required proof of US citizenship for voters and mandated voters to present identification when casting their ballot.

But on Tuesday, after winning re-election, he said backlash from voters was bigger than just one piece of legislation.

“Well, I think in every election, it’s never any one thing”, Thune told reporters. “I think it was a combination of things and, most importantly, it was the cost of living for the American people”.

The Republican leader had previously tried to raise the alarm on affordability, including rising global energy prices, in the lead-up to the midterms. During a Fox News interview in September, Thune said Trump’s war in Iran, which he once said would not be a “long-term thing”, had “trumped everything else” for US voters.

He has also emphasised Israel’s right to self-defence and criticised policies that pressure the Israeli military’s operations.

“Both the president and the Democrat leader are entitled to their personal strategic opinions and their personal opinions on Israel’s leadership,” Thune said in response to remarks by former President Joe Biden and then-Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer in 2024. “What they are not entitled to is to attempt to dictate the election process or the strategic planning of a sovereign nation.”

Over the next two years, Thune will have to contend with a White House that has indicated it wants to double down on its most controversial policies while working to prevent further Republican losses in the 2028 election. He will also have to work with a Democratic-controlled Congress if Republicans hope to advance any legislation.

Thune, however, said he is looking forward to the “important work” that lies ahead.

“I’m proud of what this Republican team has accomplished together,” he said. “We remain united in our commitment to advancing conservative priorities, working with President Trump and our colleagues in the House, and holding the line against Democrats’ efforts to enact their far-left, liberal agenda”.
news.content:
با وجود درخواست برخی قانونگذاران جمهوری خواه برای ارزیابی شکست میان دوره ای حزب به دموکرات ها، جمهوری خواه بدون مخالفت رقابت کرد. جمهوری خواهان در سنای ایالات متحده در حالی که آنها برای از دست دادن قدرت آماده می شوند، جان تون را مجدداً به رهبری حزب خود در سال های پایانی ریاست جمهوری دونالد ترامپ انتخاب کردند. تون در بیانیه‌ای پس از رأی‌گیری گفت: «من از فرصتی که امروز با همکارانم به‌عنوان یک گفتگوی باز، صادقانه و شفاف داشتم، قدردانی می‌کنم، قانون‌گذار داکوتای جنوبی در جلسه‌ای پشت درهای بسته در کنگره آمریکا در روز سه‌شنبه، حمایت جمهوری‌خواهان سنا را به دست آورد – حتی در حالی که برخی امیدوار بودند رای رهبری را برای بررسی اشتباهات انتخابات هفته گذشته به تأخیر بیندازند.» من مفتخرم که از اعتماد و حمایت مستمر آنها برای رهبری کنفرانس جمهوریخواهان سنا در کنگره 120 برخوردار هستم.
برخلاف دو سال پیش، زمانی که تون با دو تن از جمهوری‌خواهان دیگرش برای جایگزینی سناتور میچ مک‌کانل به عنوان رهبر سنای حزب رقابت کرد، روز سه‌شنبه بدون مخالفت برای این نقش شرکت کرد. سناتور جاش هاولی پس از رای‌گیری به خبرنگاران گفت که اگر جمهوری‌خواهان سنا بیشتر صبر می‌کردند، «شاید» یک رقیب وجود داشت. من فقط فکر می کنم که ما چیزهای زیادی داریم که باید در مورد آنها فکر کنیم، و فکر می کنم که برای عجله کردن در این مورد و تأیید همه رهبری یکسان، چه پیامی می فرستد؟ جمهوریخواه میسوری گفت. سناتور جمهوریخواه ران جانسون، که نامه ای را برای تاخیر در رای گیری منتشر کرد، گفت که تلاش کرده است تصمیمات رهبری را به تعویق بیندازد.

این اعتصاب کمتر از سه هفته به برگزاری انتخابات سراسری زودهنگام در اسپانیا برپا شده است
news.originalContent:
اولین اعتصاب سراسری در چهارده سال باعث اختلالاتی در سراسر اسپانیا شد. کارخانه‌ها و بندرها تعطیل شدند و خدمات حمل‌ونقل عمومی نیز به‌شدت کاهش یافتند.

اتحادیه‌های کارگری به کمبود مسکن مقرون‌به‌صرفه و افزایش هزینه‌های زندگی اعتراض دارند.

در برخی مناطق، پلیس با تظاهرکنندگانی درگیر شد که راه‌ها را مسدود کرده بودند.

این اعتصاب کمتر از سه هفته به برگزاری انتخابات سراسری زودهنگام در اسپانیا برپا شده است. پدرو سانچز، نخست‌وزیر چپگرا، پس از آنکه پارلمان طرح او را برای اصلاحات در حوزه مسکن تصویب نکرد، اعلام انتخابات کرد.

بزرگترین اعتراض و اختلال‌ها در مادرید، پایتخت، و شمال شرقی کاتالونیا که راه‌ها ساعت‌ها بسته شدند.

پپه آلوارز، رئیس اتحادیه بزرگ کارگری بزرگ یو‌جی‌تی، گفت که مشارکت در اعتصاب گسترده همراه بوده اما کنفدراسیون سازمان‌های تجاری اسپانیا گفت که مشارکت بسته به منطقه و صنف «کم و ناهمگون» بوده است.

وزارت کشور گفت ده‌ها نفر به دلیل حوادث مختلف بازداشت شده‌اند و گزارش‌ها از اسپانیا حاکی از حملاتی به بنگاه‌های املاک و مستغلات است.

این اعتصاب به دنبال اعتراضات گسترده به گرانی اجاره و افزایش هزینه‌های زندگی است که پس از بیرون راندن  ماریکارمن آباسکال ۸۷ ساله از آپارتمانی در مادرید که هفت دهه در آن زندگی کرده بود، آغاز شد. او چند هفته بعد در بیمارستان درگذشت.

اجاره مسکن در پایتخت اسپانیا در سال‌های اخیر به شدت افزایش یافته است. طبق گزارش‌ بعضی از بنگاه‌های املاک، اجاره یک آپارتمان ۵۰ متری در مادرید در ماه اکتبر به طور متوسط ماهی ۱۱۷۰ یورو بوده است درحالی‌که میانگین حقوق ناخالص ماهانه در اسپانیا حدود ۲۴۶۰ یورو است، تقریباً نصف میانگین حقوق ناخالص و بسیار بالاتر از ۳۰ درصد حقوق که اغلب کارشناسان مسکن و مؤسسات دولتی به‌عنوان اجاره مناسب توصیه می‌کنند.

پدرو سانچز ماه گذشته پس از آنکه پارلمان طرح او برای اصلاحات مسکن را تصویب نکرد، انتخابات زودهنگام اعلام کرد.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

اسپانیا از سال ۲۰۱۲ شاهد اعتصاب عمومی نبوده است.

اعتصاب‌های قبلی هم برای دولت مشکل‌ساز بودند اما این اعتصاب متفاوت است. پدرو سانچز و وزرایش حتی کارگران را تشویق کرده‌اند که کار را کنار بگذارند و مسکن ارزان مطالبه کنند.

او در شبکه‌های اجتماعی با ستایش از کسانی که در اعتصاب‌های قبلی شرکت کرده بودند، نوشت: «روزی هشت ساعت کار، حقوق بازنشستگی، بهداشت همگانی... اینها پیروزی‌های جمعی بودند.»

در مقابل حزب محافظه کار مردم دولت را متهم کرده که قصد دارد از اعتصاب به عنوان ابزاری برای بهره‌برداری‌های انتخاباتی استفاده کند.

آلبرتو نونیز فیخو، رهبر حزب مردم، این اعتصاب سراسری را «مزخرف» خواند و اتحادیه‌ها را «مافیا» و «آشغال» توصیف کرد.

این حزب در نظرسنجی‌ها پیشتاز است و میگل ته‌یادو، سخنگوی این حزب، دولت را متهم کرد که با بهره‌برداری از این اعتصاب، رأی‌دهندگان را از تشکیل یک دولت راست‌گرا می‌ترساند.

در حال حاضر به نظر می‌رسد این حزب محتمل‌ترین پیروز انتخابات ۲۹ نوامبر باشد.

پدرو سانچز در پاسخ به تلویزیون اسپانیا گفت: «آنچه واقعاً مزخرف است زیر سؤال بردن حق اعتصاب کارگران است.»

news.summary: قاتلان جمعی — همراه با قاتلان زندانی، کودک و پلیس — افکار خود را با Daily Caller در مورد تصمیم گوین نیوسام، فرماندار دموکرات کالیفرنیا، برای تخفیف مجازات زندانیان محکوم به اعدام در سراسر ایالت به اشتراک گذاشتند. اندکی پس از انتخابات میان‌دوره‌ای 2026، نیوسام مجازات همه 548 زندانی
news.originalContent:
Mass murderers — along with prison, child, and cop killers — shared their thoughts with the Daily Caller about Democratic California Gov. Gavin Newsom’s decision to commute the sentences of death row inmates across the state.

Shortly after the 2026 midterm election, Newsom commuted the sentences of all 548 inmates on California’s death row, in what was the largest mass commutation of death sentences in U.S. history. However, the California Constitution requires the state Supreme Court to review clemency grants for the vast majority of inmates who have been on multiple counts. (RELATED: STATE OF MONDAY: Gavin Newsom Plays Populist — Behind The Curtain He’s A Uniparty Darling)

The six felons who spoke with the Caller offered differing views on Newsom’s decision, his political ambitions, and how a commuted sentence could change their lives.

When asked whether Newsom’s act of grace was the beginning of a potential presidential campaign, Ka Pasasouk told the Caller, “I hope he does.”

“If you do run for president, I mean, it just gives me more hope because if you could commute death sentences, you could give people a chance to go home,” said Pasasouk, who was condemned to death after killing a rival and three witnesses outside a Los Angeles boarding home in 2012.

Although Pasasouk admits he has made a “mistake,” he said he is ready to move forward and would love to see his grandchild and go fishing.

More realistically, the man who didn’t learn to read or write until he was on death row said that if the commutation did go through, he would no longer have to be isolated or constantly shackled. He would also be able to socialize, join group programs, and participate in personal development opportunities.

<> on August 15, 2016 in San Quentin, California.

In contrast, one of the 34 inmates on death row for killing a police officer said he accepted long ago that he would die in prison because of California’s “broken system.”

“It was never gonna happen,” he added, explaining he initially welcomed the prospect of death over a life in prison when he was arrested more than two decades ago. Over time, however, he accepted that California had not executed anyone since 2006.

Before stepping out to walk his prison-issued dog, the inmate said he would never vote for Newsom because of their political differences. Nevertheless, he expressed a “newfound respect for him” for following through on the commutations, despite believing the decision might “hurt” Newsom’s future political chances.

“I deserve to be in prison,” he said, wishing he could apologize to the family of the person he killed but believing doing so would only reopen old wounds.

Another inmate, Edward Charles, who was sentenced for the 1994 murder of his parents and brother, declined to discuss the commutation but told the Caller he would write Newsom directly.

However, not everyone welcomed the decision. Some inmates viewed the commutations as “wrong.”

Miguel Crespo, who was serving a life sentence for second-degree murder, was later condemned to death for binding, gagging, torturing, and killing his “transgender woman” cellmate within eight hours of being paired together.

Despite Newsom offering platitudes against violence and hate toward the “trans and gender non-conforming people taken from us by violence and discrimination,” Crespo is also eligible for a commuted sentence.

Crespo criticized what he sees as politically motivated commutations, telling the Caller that Newsom’s “political [ambitions] to become what he wish is at [innocent] people price,” adding that he is “callous and [indifferent] to the [suffering] of others.”

Michael “Santos” Walters also opposed the commutations, describing Newsom’s post-election decision as “all political,” “suspicious,” and hypocritical.

Christopher Henriquez, who murdered his pregnant wife and two-year-old daughter, said that despite spending more than 30 years in prison, he has “little say so over this system that holds me.”

“As far as the decision made by Newsom,” Henriquez told the Caller, “with the way things have been going for me in this overall horrible situation, either way I will most likely die in prison. Whether that be by the state or natural causes, etc.” (RELATED: Literal Dead Guy Leading In Too Close To Call Election)

The family killer continued, “My life has been one of many bad decisions, and the consequences that have followed. As I struggle with my addictions and flawed personality, at 55 I learned: all we should want people to remember of us is the good that we give the universe of humanity. “

(Photo by Andrew Harnik/Getty Images)

Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin was put on the spot over comments suggesting the administration be open to an immigration deal with Democrats.

During a Tuesday interview on Fox News’ The Ingraham Angle, host Laura Ingraham challenged Mullin over his openness to working with Democrats on immigration, citing a long history of Republican lawmakers trying to strike immigration deals with the opposing party. (RELATED: EXCLUSIVE: White House Scrambles After Trump Again Floats Amnesty Deal With Democrats)

In reference to the failed proposed deals, Ingraham named Oklahoma Republican Sen. James Lankford, former Florida Sen. and current Secretary of State Marco Rubio, former Arizona Sen. John McCain and former President George W. Bush.

🚨 JUST NOW: Laura Ingraham DESTROYS Markwayne Miullin LIVE ON FOX for pushing for "LEGAL STATUS" for DACA illegals LAURA: "Why would ANY idea be floated to work with the Democrats on an issue that is their HOLY GRAIL?!" "It seems like EVERY TIME Republicans feel like they’re running into a rough spot, they rush to some type of immigration deal with a party that you yourself has said has NO INTEREST in lowering immigration, legal immigration, or enforcing the laws as they exist." "Why did you float DACA, Mr. Secretary? Why is THAT the message for you guys this election?!" — @IngrahamAngle MULLIN: "… some of them may not even speak English or never even lived in their country!" WHAT KIND OF ARGUMENT IS THAT?! NO AMNESTY. PERIOD.

Ingraham argued that Republicans repeatedly turn to immigration compromises whenever they face political difficulties, even as Democrats show little interest in lowering immigration levels or enforcing existing laws.

“So why would any idea be floated to work with Democrats on an issue that is their holy grail as well?” she asked the secretary.

Mullin pushed back, arguing that the specifics of any potential agreement would matter. He said that making people who entered the U.S. illegally legal would be a nonstarter, but suggested there could be room to discuss reforms involving amnesty and the country’s ports of entry.

The Fox News host interrupted to question why Mullin had specifically floated DACA as a possible area of discussion, asking, “Why is that the message for you guys this election?” (RELATED: Deportation Data Dispute Sparks Another Oversight Project Lawsuit Against Trump DHS)

Mullin defended the idea of considering a legal status for certain DACA recipients, arguing that many were brought to the U.S. as children through no fault of their own.

“DACA applies to children that were brought to this country at no fault of their own. Yes, but they were brought here at no fault of their own. And some of them may not even speak English or never even lived in their country,” Mullin said. “I think that there is a part that we could say, listen, you’re not going to become citizens because you weren’t born here. But is there a path for you to be legal.”

The secretary acknowledged that such an agreement was a long shot, noting that President Donald Trump attempted to strike a similar deal in 2016 but Democrats did not take him up on the offer.

He also stressed that the administration would not pursue any agreement without first securing support from Republican voters, saying, “We are going to make sure our base is with us on it.”

Ingraham immediately challenged that assertion.

“They are not with you. They’re not, I’m just saying this,” she told Mullin.

Mullin added that Trump would not sign an agreement unless it was in the best interest of the country and the Republican Party.

Ingraham warned that any concessions made under a Republican administration could eventually be undermined by a future Democratic administration, arguing that Republicans might not remain in power long enough to ensure the terms of a deal were upheld.

“Maybe if we’ll get that for that, maybe that would kind of seem good. Problem is you’re not going to be in office. Maybe in two years or four years or six years,” Ingraham said.

Amnesty will NEVER be on the table.

She questioned whether future Democratic administrations would respect the rule of law or uphold any immigration agreement reached with Republicans, arguing that Democrats could simply reverse course once they regained power.

Ingraham further warned that Democrats could “open up the floodgates again and everyone is going to come in, plus the people you regulate are already going to be here,” arguing that there was no guarantee Democrats would negotiate in good faith. (RELATED: EXCLUSIVE: More Foreign Nationals Come Under ICE Scrutiny For Alleged Illegal Voting)

Mullin acknowledged that the possibility had to be considered, while also pointing to Democrats’ calls to defund U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) as evidence that Republicans could not trust them on immigration enforcement.

Mullin added that Trump has the final say and can veto legislation that doesn’t align with his priorities.

(Photo by Brandon Bell/Getty Images)

In Austin, Texas, last week, a software engineer named Trever—recently arrived from the San Francisco area after “the vibes got bad”—stood outside a responsibly sourced coffee shop and explained to a local that the city’s rising property taxes, homelessness, drug use, and the new smash-and-grab at the Whole Foods “troubled him.”

Trever had voted, he added proudly, for the feel-good Democrat candidates last week, James Talerico, who promised housing mandates, expanded social services, affordability, free healthcare, and unicorns. When the local asked whether any of this sounded familiar, Trevor just stared blankly.

If you think Trevor had a bad week, just remember all the other Californians who moved to Texas to escape the left-wing politics that ruined that state. If California got even more woke, Vanilla Wafers would come with a Trigger Warning. I paid $2.84 for gas yesterday. Gas prices are still so high, and traffic is so bad in California; kidnap victims are no longer driven to a second location. (RELATED: California’s High-Price Petroleum Virus May Spread Across The West, Analyst Says)

Southerners are concerned. We may never win another election if Californians do not stay in California. I almost voted for Democrat judges because I may want to murder someone someday, and it would be a bummer to have to go to prison for it.

Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed is declaring Michigan the “Arab Capital of America.” Well, Sharia Law might not be all bad for us guys; my wife has been getting a bit mouthy.

El Sayed is the new darling of the left. He will be nominated for an Oscar for Best Animated Short. El Sayed might as well name his state Michigan-istan. But I am not worried. Upon hearing this, Israel has started to convince Trump that Michigan-istan is only weeks away from developing a nuclear weapon.

For more than a decade, people have been voting with their U-Hauls. Americans have been conducting a large, unsupervised experiment in political geography. People leave California, New York, Illinois, and New Jersey because the taxes are high, the streets are less safe, the schools are terrible, and the housing market has been regulated into unaffordability. They move to Texas, Florida, Tennessee, and the Carolinas. Census numbers show the pattern clearly: blue states lose hundreds of thousands of residents a year to red ones. The movers cite cost of living, crime, and quality of life. They do not, as a rule, cite a sudden conversion to limited government.

The least surprising part: property taxes in the new suburbs start climbing to fund the expanded services the newcomers requested. Crime rates in previously quiet cities tick upward after local prosecutors adopt the “root causes” approach that emptied jails. School boards that once focused on reading scores discover “equity frameworks.” Housing becomes more expensive again once zoning and environmental reviews return in force. The newcomers look at the numbers, look at the crime map, and declare that something has gone wrong—somehow blaming Republicans, or “late-stage capitalism.” (RELATED: Democrat DA Pushed Racial Equity As Crime Spiked Before Horrific Train Stabbing)

What they rarely say is that the policies produced the same results in the old place. California’s housing shortage was not caused by a shortage of compassionate people; it was caused by decades of rules that made it illegal to build enough homes. New York’s subway crime problem was not mysterious; it tracked the decision to stop enforcing certain laws. Illinois’ pension crisis was not an act of God; it was the predictable outcome of promising benefits without funding them. When the same leftist levers are pulled in a new state, it produces the same output.

One problem is that the GOP is now the Trump show. He will have two 4-year terms, punctuated by Biden’s 22 percent cumulative inflation for his four years. The worst halftime show ever. Trump has killed more RINOs than Teddy Roosevelt.

And there were other mistakes: a war of choice, balking on the Epstein Files release, bragging when he should be explaining, and being tone deaf on abortion. In Red States now, if you want an abortion, you still have choices: the Moderna, JNJ, or Pfizer vaccine.

Not to worry, sources close to the White House tell me that Trump will work all this out in his 3rd term.

The midterms simply accelerated a process that was already visible in county-level data and moving-company statistics. The destinations are becoming more like the origins, one school board and one prosecutor’s race at a time. The people who left will, in a few years, have new reasons to leave again.

A libertarian op-ed humorist and award-winning author, Ron does commentary on radio and TV. He can be contacted at Ron@RonaldHart.com or @RonaldHart on Twitter.
